question: Should `/status` display cumulative transcript-backed session cost now, and if so should the linked PR use a bounded/precomputed aggregate rather than full transcript scans on default status paths?
rationale: The user value is clear, but cost display semantics and status fast-path performance are product/UX tradeoffs that automation should not settle while the linked PR remains blocked on that design.

options.title: Land bounded cumulative cost
options.body: Require the linked PR to use a bounded, cached, or maintained aggregate for session cost and land it once review and mergeability are clean.

options.title: Accept exact full scans
options.body: Allow exact transcript scans in default status output as an intentional responsiveness tradeoff with documented expectations.

options.title: Defer until aggregate storage
options.body: Keep this issue open and pause the linked PR if the right solution needs broader session aggregate storage work first.

recommendation.title: Land bounded cumulative cost
recommendation.body: Require the linked PR to use a bounded, cached, or maintained aggregate for session cost and land it once review and mergeability are clean.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent status rendering and model/status wiring history makes this person a good routing candidate for the status UX and fast-path tradeoff.
